editorial.headline: Independent Professional Certification: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 85694 covers independent, impartial certification of individual competence—open to full foreign ownership nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Independent Professional Certification is a business activity built around a narrow proposition: judging an individual’s competence through competency testing, then providing certification on an independent and impartial basis. The emphasis on independence matters: the scope distinguishes this service from professional certification conducted by associations. It is an assessment-based service centred on a person’s competence. Its stated scope reaches independent professional certification in sport and services certifying the competence of technical electricity workers. That combination makes the activity specific in method while allowing application across the areas named in its scope.

The record opens this activity to Micro, Small, Medium and Large business scales. The relevant registrant is therefore an operator actually delivering the defined certification service, rather than simply participating in the professional field being assessed. At every permitted scale, the essential character remains the same: competence is tested, certification is delivered, and the process is independent and impartial. The scale range gives the activity room to be organised from a smaller enterprise through to a large operation without loosening that central definition.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA: open. The foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, meaning the record permits full foreign ownership of this activity at the national level. This is not a partial foreign-share allowance disguised as an open category; the stated ceiling is the full 100%. The national PMA basis cited in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign investor reading the classification carefully, the national position is direct: independent professional certification under this scope is open to PMA up to full ownership.

Bali’s position is also clear, though it turns on the stated risk treatment. The record says the activity is not blocked by the provincial moratorium because, at Large scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High/High. That places it outside Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium rule for PMA registrations in Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. Its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The honest conclusion is straightforward: this activity is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership and remains registrable for PMA in Bali, rather than being barred by the moratorium.
